children: Expanded portfolio delivers flexible AI and HPC solutions from data center to edge
address density, serviceability and performance needs
ASUS showcases AMD Instinct and upcoming Intel GPU D-series (Crescent Island) system options for demanding applications
NVIDIA-accelerated desktop systems and industrial edge platforms broaden deployment flexibility

CHICAGO, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- At SC26, ASUS unveils a unified AI Factory blueprint that gives enterprises the flexibility to build AI infrastructure around their workloads, performance targets, and deployment needs. Spanning AMD, Intel and NVIDIA platforms — from rack-scale AI systems and enterprise servers to edge computing — ASUS brings architectural choice together with integrated engineering, automated manufacturing, rigorous validation, and lifecycle support. With volume shipments of its latest rack-scale AI systems underway this quarter, ASUS demonstrates how it turns next-generation computing architectures into deployment-ready infrastructure, helping enterprises move from AI ambition to real-world implementation with greater confidence, consistency, and scalability.
Next-gen power redefines value for enterprise
For computationally intensive enterprise deployments, ASUS showcases its lineup powered by the

processor family, giving organizations more control over compute density, storage capacity and rack space. The dual-socket 1U RS700A-E14B-R16U combines PCIe® 6.0 connectivity with support for up to 16 E3.S drives for demanding data and compute services. Single-socket alternatives address different deployment priorities: the 2U RS520A-E14B-R12U offers flexible GPU and NVMe configurations, while the compact 1U RS500A-E14B-R12U concentrates high-speed storage and DC-MHS serviceability in a smaller footprint. At the accelerator level, ESC8000A-E13P supports AMD Instinct™ MI350P, and the air-cooled XA AM3A-E13 integrates eight AMD Instinct MI355X™ GPUs for compute-intensive model development and scientific simulation. Across both CPU and GPU offerings, ASUS emphasizes configuration flexibility and serviceability to help customers tailor infrastructure to budget, facility and application requirements.
Expanding architectural choice for enterprise data centers

For Intel-based infrastructure, ASUS features two dual-socket Intel Xeon® 6 servers built on the service-friendly DC-MHS architecture. The RS700-E12-RS4U combines dense dual-socket Intel Xeon 6 CPU resources with four NVMe drive bays for compact, performance-oriented installations, while the 2U RS720-E12-RS12U offers up to 12 NVMe bays and extensive I/O expansion to accommodate growing data and connectivity demands. Both platforms support infrastructure consolidation, virtualization and business-critical applications, with modular design and tool-less access helping streamline maintenance. ASUS also previews the upcoming ESC8000-E13P server based on Intel's next-generation server processor codenamed Diamond Rapids, featuring Intel GPU D-series, formerly code-named Crescent Island to broaden future accelerator options for organizations evaluating their AI computing strategies.
Extending intelligent computing from the data center to the edge

AI value is ultimately realized where data is created. ASUS extends intelligent computing from the data center to the edge with the PE3000N and PE6000G systems, engineered for robotics, industrial automation, and responsive on-site processing. At the deskside, the ASUS Ascent GX10 and ExpertCenter Pro ET900N G3 bring NVIDIA-accelerated computing directly to developers and enterprise teams, enabling them to prototype, refine, and run models locally before scaling to larger infrastructure.

What sets the ASUS approach apart is the single engineering, validation, and support model that covers every architecture and form factor. Customers no longer need to manage multiple vendor relationships or inconsistent processes as their AI environments evolve from edge devices to enterprise servers to rack-scale systems. By combining architectural choice with automated manufacturing, thorough validation, and full-lifecycle services — from initial design and commissioning through sustained operations — ASUS helps organizations build AI infrastructure that remains dependable, efficient, and ready to scale, whatever the workload and wherever it runs.
Visitors can explore ASUS computing solutions at Booth #2234 during SC26 at McCormick Place in Chicago.
ASUS servers are available worldwide. Availability of individual products and configurations may vary by region. Please contact your local ASUS representative for further information.
